The trailing P/E ratio on the S&P 500 is now 25, above the global average of 17 and well above the 11-12 average P/Es for emerging markets stocks in China and Latin America. A review of yields tells a similar story. The current dividend yield for the S&P 500 is 1.0%, versus the global average of 2.1% and European and Latin American yields of 3%-4%. Investors generally are willing to pay a higher price for North American securities for several reasons, including the transparency of the U.S. financial system as well as the liquidity of U.S. markets. What's more, global returns can be volatile across individual countries, given currency, security, political, and geopolitical risks. Indeed, U.S. stocks (ETF SPY) have outperformed Europe, Australasia, and the Far East (EAFE, and ETF EFA) over the past five years. The tide turned a bit in 2025, as investors responded to the uncertainty over U.S. trade policy and as global central banks lowered rates. Last year, foreign stocks were up 28% while U.S. stocks rose 16%. Meanwhile, the outperformance of emerging markets over domestic markets has continued in 2026.
